newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH KOMERCNI TO LOWER REFERENCE RATE TO 16.4 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH KOMERCNI TO LOWER REFERENCE RATE TO 16.4 PCT.

text.p: Komercni banka a.s., the Czech Republic's largest commercial bank, said on Tuesday that it was lowering its reference lending rate to 16.4 percent from 17.6 percent, effective July 9.
The bank added in a statement that it was also lowering its base lending rate to 15.7 percent from a previous 16.75 percent, also effective July 9.
Czech interest rates skyrocketed in mid-May when the central bank tightened its grip on the market in an attempt to save the crown from a wave of speculative short-selling.
The central bank hiked its main interest rates and cut off market liquidity, pushing interbank rates as high as 200 percent, before it was forced to freely float the crown on May 27.
Since then, rates have come down with the central bank's Lombard rate currently sitting at 23 percent after rising as high as 50 percent.
